# libgooglepinyin (vendored) — upstream revision and patches

## Source

* Repository: <https://salsa.debian.org/input-method-team/libgooglepinyin.git>
* Branch / commit: `upstream` @ `b856da0ba1d8b7399d365fb3e91092a19a0551e8`
  (recorded in `UPSTREAM_REVISION.txt`, generated by the vendoring step)
* Licence: Apache-2.0 (see `LICENSE` in the repository root for the project,
  and the per-file headers for upstream).

`src/` and `include/` are copied verbatim from upstream. `tools/` holds only
`pinyinime_dictbuilder.cpp`, the offline model builder, so that
`tools/gen_dict.py` can rebuild `dict_pinyin.dat` without network access.

## Patches

Upstream is unchanged except for patch **P0**, which is one guarded `#define`
in `include/dictdef.h`. Everything else is done from the build system, so a
`diff -ru` against upstream stays readable.

| # | Where | Change | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **P0** | `include/dictdef.h` | `___BUILD_MODEL___` is now only defined when `PINYINIME_RUNTIME_ONLY` is *not* defined. The firmware compiles with `-DPINYINIME_RUNTIME_ONLY`. | Upstream hard-enables the model builder, which drags `dictbuilder.cpp`, `utf16reader.cpp` and the raw word list into the firmware image. The host toolchain still builds the model (no macro defined), so one source tree serves both. |
| P1 | build system | `-Wl,--wrap=malloc,--wrap=free,--wrap=calloc,--wrap=realloc` on the `libgooglepinyin` component, implemented by `src/core/ime_alloc.c` (PSRAM first, internal RAM fallback). | Keeps the ~2 MB of dictionary tables out of internal RAM, where the SPI DMA draw buffers must live. Was "edit every malloc" in the original plan; a linker wrap needs no upstream edits. |
| P2 | `port/pinyinime_compat.h`, force-included with `-include` | On toolchains without `<pthread.h>` (MinGW, used by `test_apps/host_core_test`) the mutex macro surface maps onto a `std::recursive_mutex`. ESP-IDF keeps its own pthread. | Upstream uses `pthread_mutex_t`, `PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER` and `pthread_mutex_trylock`; only the host toolchain lacks them. |
| P3 | no code change | The dictionary is loaded with `fopen`/`fread` into `malloc`ed buffers, both upstream. The zero-copy mmap idea from the plan is not needed: the read-only VFS (`src/data/ime_dict_vfs.c`) already lets the engine `fopen` the flash partition directly. | — |
| P4 | `port/pinyinime_compat.h` | Same shim as P2 covers `sync.cpp` / `userdict.cpp`. | — |
| P5 | not applicable | Upstream `userdict.cpp` already writes back only from `close_dict()`; our user dictionary work (stage S5) will add the explicit flush policy on top. | — |
| P6 | no code change | Upstream's runtime `printf`s are all behind `const bool kPrintDebugX = false`, so a release build is silent. | Verified by inspection; see the grep in the S1 commit. |
| P7 | build system | `-w` on the `libgooglepinyin` component only; our own sources keep the project warning level. | Keeps third-party warnings out of the build log without touching upstream. |

## API notes discovered while porting

* The exported C++ API lives in namespace `ime_pinyin`; `pinyinime.h` wraps the
  declarations in `extern "C"` *around* the namespace, so the symbols are still
  C++-mangled. `src/core/ime_engine_port.cpp` is the only translation unit that
  is allowed to include the upstream headers.
* `im_search(const char *sps_buf, size_t sps_len)` takes the spelling buffer as
  **plain ASCII bytes**, not UTF-16, and `sps_len` counts characters.
  `pi'ao` is accepted and decoded as two syllables, which is what the 分词 key
  relies on (verified on the host: `pi'ao` → 皮奥, `piao` → 票).
* `MatrixSearch::init()` rejects a **NULL** user dictionary path even though it
  tolerates a path that does not exist, so `ime_engine_open()` substitutes an
  empty string for "keep the user dictionary in RAM only".
* `im_get_predicts()` uses a C++ reference parameter, so it cannot be called
  from C; `ime_engine_predict()` / `ime_engine_predict_item()` wrap it.
* Upstream has **no double pinyin support** at all (no `SetDpScheme`, no scheme
  table). Stage S5 will therefore implement the scheme mapping inside
  `src/core/ime_scheme.c` and feed the engine a full pinyin string.
